title: Plus One
prompt:
`digits` represents a non-negative integer, most-significant digit first. Add one and return the resulting digits.

**Example**: `[1,2,3]` → `[1,2,4]`; `[9,9]` → `[1,0,0]`.

Add from the right, carrying; if every digit was 9, the result grows by one digit.
hints: When does adding one change more than the last digit?
Only when that digit is 9. Scan right to left: a digit below 9 gets incremented and you return immediately, while a 9 becomes 0 and the carry moves left.
If the carry falls off the front (every digit was 9), return a new array one longer: `res[0] = 1`, the rest zeros.

solution.explanation: Adding one only turns a run of trailing 9s into 0s and bumps the first non-9 digit. The number only gets longer when every digit is 9 (99 → 100), and that fresh array is all zeros except a leading 1. O(n) time, O(1) extra space except in the all-9s case.
